QuidelOrtho Investigation Initiated: Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC Investigates the Officers and Directors of QuidelOrtho Corporation - QDEL

QuidelOrtho Investigation Initiated: Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC Investigates the Officers and Directors of QuidelOrtho Corporation - QDEL

PR Newswire

NEW ORLEANS, Nov. 20, 2026

NEW ORLEANS, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Former Attorney General of Louisiana, Charles C. Foti, Jr., Esq., a partner at the law firm of Kahn Swick & Foti, LLC ("KSF"), announces that KSF has commenced an investigation into QuidelOrtho Corporation ("QuidelOrtho" or the "Company") (NasdaqGS: QDEL).

According to a securities class action filed against the Company, internal reports and accounts from former employees described serious and unresolved problems with the Company's flagship test, the Savanna Respiratory Viral Panel 4 ("RVP4"). The lawsuit alleges that the European launch was plagued by high rates of invalid test results, device failures, and mounting customer complaints, with between 60% and 80% of European customer feedback being negative. The complaint further alleges that Savanna's invalid test rate ran between 10% and 30%, far above the industry standard of 1% to 2%, and that roughly one in four instruments sold in Europe had to be replaced. According to the lawsuit, the product could not consistently meet the FDA's sensitivity requirements, and manufacturing yields fell far below internal targets, with former employees describing scrap rates of 50% to 80%. The lawsuit also alleges that the Company doubled its endemic COVID-19 revenue guidance, from $150 million–$200 million to $200 million–$400 million, without supporting data, even as internal reports showed declining sales and accumulating inventory.

KSF's investigation is focusing on whether QuidelOrtho's officers and/or directors of  breached their fiduciary duties to its shareholders or otherwise violated state or federal laws. 

If you have information that would assist KSF in its investigation, or have been a long-term holder of QuidelOrtho's shares and would like to discuss your legal rights, you may, without obligation or cost to you, call toll-free at 1-833-538-3606 or email KSF Managing Partner Lewis Kahn (lewis.kahn@ksfcounsel.com), or visit https://www.ksfcounsel.com/cases/nasdaqgs-qdel to learn more.

data.title: Tech outages are rattling Americans so much that they're stockpiling cash and supplies
data.description:
By Genna Contino and Andrew Keshner

A lack of clarity from world leaders is prompting some people to prepare for the worst

Consumers have been stockpiling food and bottled water in the wake of a nationwide ground stop and a string of tech outages.

When Shakeela McNeely heard about the nationwide ground stop at airports Friday, just a day after a major Microsoft outage, she started going through her emergency checklist.

The 36-year-old from Concord, N.C., generally keeps a small stockpile of bottled water, food and dog food at this time of year, as hurricane season wraps up. She also gardens, keeps chickens and has fruit trees growing in her yard.

The one thing missing from her checklist was cash. McNeely said she feels comfortable having about $500 on hand but put off going to the ATM over the weekend. But when she heard the news about service disruptions at Chase (JPM) and other major U.S. banks on Monday, she rushed to the nearest ATM. It was down.

"I would like to get into canning and preserves and things like that," McNeely told MarketWatch. "But I'm not like a doomsday prepper, where I feel like I have to have a bunker."

McNeely was able to withdraw cash from her credit union, but she's still suspicious about the back-to-back tech disruptions.

"I do think we're under a cyberattack. The war is one of the main reasons they feel like they lost the midterms," McNeely said, referring to Republicans' losses up and down the ballot earlier this month. "And now they're trying to wrap it up, and Iran is retaliating."

Vice President J.D. Vance has tried to assure Americans there's "no crisis coming down," while still noting that it's good to be prepared. "What we want to do is make sure that we prevent the worst outcome, but we're also prepared for the worst outcomes," Vance said on "The Ingraham Angle" on Fox News on Monday.

President Donald Trump, however, told a Fox News reporter in Shenzen, China, on Wednesday that "these are individual events," and said people who are stockpiling should "relax." In the United Kingdom, the government is urging residents to stockpile three days' worth of food and water to prepare for emergencies such as severe weather and cyberattacks.

Dive deeper: Washington is scrambling to get to the bottom of the growing number of tech outages across America

Additional outages, including at the National Security Agency on Tuesday, along with a lack of clarity from world leaders, are prompting some Americans to prepare for the worst, according to behavioral economists. While some like McNeely are rushing to withdraw cash, others are clearing out the shelves at Costco (COST).

Some Americans' urge to stockpile may be fed by a slow-building anxiety about humanity's fate since September, when artificial-intelligence researchers and financial firms acknowledged that AI tools could lead to human extinction. Then the midterm results threw markets into turmoil by calling into question the future of the AI trade that has powered stock-market gains over the past few years.

How people respond to uncertainty varies greatly depending on their personal risk tolerance, behavioral economists say, and those who are uncomfortable with uncertainty are more likely to go into prep mode.

But one economics professor thinks what people are feeling now goes beyond uncertainty.

"Uncertainty is one thing. That's when you don't know what's going to happen, but you have some sense of what the possibilities are," said Alexander Smith, a professor at the Worcester Polytechnic Institute who specializes in behavioral economics. "Right now we have something more than that. We have ambiguity, because people aren't even sure what could happen."

This can push people to take extreme measures, like withdrawing all the cash in their bank accounts.

"People like to hold cash because it gives them a sense of security," said Gary Zimmerman, the founder and CEO of cash-management firm MaxMyInterest. "And there's perhaps no worse financial feeling than not being able to access your hard-earned cash when you need it."

Denver financial adviser Matt Smith said he received a call from a client Monday afternoon who brought up the idea of cashing out accounts in the wake of the bank outage, the Microsoft (MSFT) disruption and the Federal Aviation Administration ground stop.

The person was never seriously considering emptying their accounts, but they wanted reassurance, Smith said. The client ultimately didn't pull any of their money.

"What's unnerving them is a growing worry about the systems their money sits on," said Smith, of West Highland Advisors. "Their view is that the downside of all this technology is access by bad actors, and they see two kinds: hackers looking to make money, and foreign threats that could target them."

Alexander Smith, the behavioral economics professor, also noted that recency bias - a cognitive bias that leads people to place more importance on recent events than historical experience - along with a growing lack of confidence in institutions is creating a compounding effect that's pushing people to start panic buying and withdrawing their cash. Only 17% of Americans trust the federal government to do what is right almost always or most of the time, a 2025 Pew Research poll found - one of the lowest levels in nearly 70 years.

"We have recent emergencies that have occurred, and people are focusing on that. And I don't think trust in institutions, broadly speaking, is quite what it has been at various points in history," he said. "If you're feeling anxiety trying to anticipate what could happen next, for some people, they're going to lean toward being overprepared."

Need help with a career or money-related problem in your life? MarketWatch's Dollar Signs advice column is here for you. Submit your questions anonymously here or write to us at dollarsigns@marketwatch.com.

-Genna Contino -Andrew Keshner

Foti, Jr., remind investors with substantial losses that they have until December 7, 2026 to file lead plaintiff applications in a securities class action lawsuit against The Chemours Company ("Chemours" or the "Company") (NYSE: CC), if they purchased or otherwise acquired the Company's securities between February 20, 2026 and August 4, 2026, inclusive (the "Class Period").  This action is pending in the United States District Court for the District of Delaware.

CLASS DEFINITION: The lawsuit seeks to recover losses on behalf of investors who purchased or otherwise acquired publicly traded Alibaba securities between May 23, 2024 and November 11, 2026, inclusive (the "Class Period"). The case is Bihan v. Alibaba Group Holding Limited et al, No. 26-cv-10158.

data.title: CCAPP Opens Registration for "Hope for the Holidays" Training on Depression, Stress, and Resilience
data.description:
CCAPP Opens Registration for "Hope for the Holidays" Training on Depression, Stress, and Resilience

CCAPP Opens Registration for "Hope for the Holidays" Training on Depression, Stress, and Resilience

PR Newswire

SACRAMENTO, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026

Virtual training led by Kristina Padilla, M.A., LAADC, Vice President of Education and Strategic Development at CCAPP, offers 2 CEUs and practical strategies for supporting mental wellness during the holiday season.

SACRAMENTO, Calif., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The California Consortium of Addiction Programs and Professionals (CCAPP) will host a specialized virtual training session, "Hope for the Holidays: Understanding Depression, Stress & Resilience During the Holiday Season," on December 2, 2026. This event provides behavioral health professionals with critical tools to navigate the seasonal increase in mental health challenges while offering 2 continuing education units (CEUs).

Registration is currently open for the virtual workshop at Workshops | CCAPP Conferences.

The program features Kristina Padilla, M.A., LAADC, Vice President of Education and Strategic Development at CCAPP and Ph.D. Student in Philosophy, who will guide participants through the identification of depression and emotional distress. The curriculum addresses specific stressors that often peak during the winter months, such as grief, loneliness, and financial strain, which can pose significant risks to individuals in recovery.

"The holidays can be a difficult time for many people, and that often gets overlooked," said Kristina Padilla, M.A., LAADC. "Not everyone experiences this season as joyful. Many people are carrying grief, stress, loneliness, or struggles with mental health and recovery. This training is an opportunity to talk openly about those experiences and offer tools that help people feel more connected, supported, and hopeful."

By focusing on resilience and awareness, CCAPP aims to equip substance use disorder counselors, peer support specialists, and supervisors with actionable strategies to support their clients and themselves during a period known for its high emotional demands.

The training session operates from 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. PST and is accessible via a remote platform. The registration fee is set at $20 for CCAPP members and $50 for non-members.

About CCAPP

The California Consortium of Addiction Programs and Professionals (CCAPP) is the largest statewide consortium of community-based substance use disorder treatment agencies, recovery organizations, and addiction-focused professionals in California. CCAPP represents thousands of behavioral health professionals and programs through advocacy, credentialing, education, workforce development, and membership services. 

For more information, visit California Consortium of Addiction Programs and Professionals

data.title: Epic Blue Marketing Contributes more than $50,000 in Professional Services Supporting Nonprofits and Startups in 2026
data.description:
Epic Blue Marketing Contributes more than $50,000 in Professional Services Supporting Nonprofits and Startups in 2026

Epic Blue Marketing Contributes more than $50,000 in Professional Services Supporting Nonprofits and Startups in 2026

PR Newswire

JACKSON, Mich., Nov. 20, 2026

JACKSON, Mich., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Since its launch, Epic Blue Marketing has made community support part of its business model, contributing professional marketing, communications and public relations services to organizations that might otherwise have limited access to those resources. In 2026 alone, the Jackson-based, women-owned firm provided $50,000 in donated and reduced-rate services to startups, nonprofits and community-focused organizations.

The support has benefited organizations including the Lean Rocket Lab, East Coast Pro, and most recently the Race for RP and the Polychondritis Foundation, helping them strengthen their communications, reach new audiences and build awareness around their missions and services.

For a small, independently owned marketing firm, making that level of professional support available is a deliberate investment in the organizations and communities it serves.

"Marketing and PR aren't luxuries for nonprofits trying to grow or make a difference, they're essential services for moving an organization forward," said Devon Roof, founder and CEO of Epic Blue Marketing. "We know not every organization has the budget to invest in this type of support, and we want to help where we can. Being a small business ourselves, we understand the importance of having people in your corner."

One of the organizations that has benefited from Epic Blue's support is the Lean Rocket Lab, a Jackson-based startup incubator, business accelerator, and coworking space that supports entrepreneurs and small businesses.

"Having a marketing partner who understands what we're trying to accomplish and is willing to jump in and help makes a real difference," said Alex Masten, director of Entrepreneurship at Lean Rocket Lab. "Organizations like ours have a lot of moving parts, and getting the right message in front of the right people is important. Epic Blue has been an outstanding resource and a partner who genuinely cares about the work we're doing."

Beyond its client partnerships and donated services, Epic Blue maintains an active presence in the Jackson community. Roof serves on the Jackson Downtown Development Authority board, and the firm values opportunities to support organizations and initiatives working to make the region a stronger place to live and do business.

Epic Blue Marketing provides strategic marketing, public relations, website development, digital marketing, social media management and communications services to businesses and organizations throughout Michigan and across the United States. Its relationship-focused approach allows the firm to work as an extension of its clients' teams, providing both strategic guidance and hands-on support.

"At the end of the day, we want to build a business that does good work, takes great care of its clients and makes a positive difference along the way," Roof said. "We're proud of the organizations we've been able to support, and we hope to continue finding ways to make our experience and resources available to those who need them."

To explore services or to learn about Epic Blue, visit www.epicblueofficial.com.

About Epic Blue Marketing
Epic Blue Marketing is a Michigan-based creative agency that helps small businesses stand out through strategic branding, digital content, and public relations. With a commitment to excellence and a passion for empowering entrepreneurs, Epic Blue offers customized services that blend vision with execution. From bold brand identities and high-impact websites to story-driven PR and content strategy, Epic Blue equips businesses to grow with clarity, confidence, and purpose. Learn more at epicblueofficial.com.

data.title: Cam Newton to Host “Tailgate Games,” a New Football-Inspired Competition Series Combining Obstacle Challenges and Tailgating
data.description:
Cam Newton to Host “Tailgate Games,” a New Football-Inspired Competition Series Combining Obstacle Challenges and Tailgating

Cam Newton and Kinsey Wolanski to offer an exclusive preview of the series during a special TikTok Live this Saturday

Former NFL MVP Cam Newton will host Tailgate Games, alongside co-host Kinsey Wolanski, a new 60-minute competition series that brings the culture of American tailgating to a series of football-inspired challenges. The series will feature male and female everyday fans competing in a series of outrageous, football-inspired challenges that combine the excitement of a traditional game show with the spirit of game day.

Ahead of the series, Newton and co-host Wolanski will lead a special TikTok Live preview on Saturday, November 21, at 4:00pm PT/7:00pm ET, giving viewers a behind-the-scenes look at the Tailgate Games arena. The livestream will feature a set tour and obstacle demonstrations by the host.

Each episode will feature contestants taking on extreme challenges inspired by tailgate traditions, including sled lanes and breakaway tables. Winners will advance to the season-ending Tailgate Bowl, where they will compete for the title of Tailgate Games champion and a $50,000 grand prize.

“Tailgate Games was developed to bring a new level of competition to one of football's most recognizable traditions. By putting everyday fans at the center, we're giving audiences a new way to experience the excitement of game day,” said Derrick W. Brown, Executive Producer of Tailgate Games.

“I'm excited to bring Tailgate Games to life. The challenges are competitive, the energy is high, and you never know what's going to happen next,” said Cam Newton, Host and Executive Producer of Tailgate Games.

The series is produced by Creator Sports Entertainment Network. Executive Producers include Derrick W. Brown, Rudy Vegliante, Travis Montaque, Royal Malloy, and Cam Newton.

Additional details regarding the series premiere and distribution will be announced at a later date. Viewers can get a first look at the series HERE and join live HERE.

data.title: Infinity Bancorp Announces Closing of $7.8 Million Subordinated Note Offering
data.description:
SANTA ANA, CA / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Infinity Bancorp (OTCQB:INFT) (the "Company"), the holding company for Infinity Bank, today announced that it completed a private placement of $7.8 million in aggregate principal amount of subordinated notes (the "Notes"). The offering consisted of $4.4 million of nonconvertible subordinated notes and $3.4 million of convertible subordinated notes.

The Notes mature on December 1, 2036. The Company has the option to redeem these notes beginning in December 2031, subject to applicable regulatory approvals.

The Notes are intended to qualify as Tier 2 regulatory capital. The Company intends to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, including support for continued organic growth and strategic initiatives.

The Notes and the common stock issuable upon conversion have not been registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or applicable state securities laws and may not be offered or sold absent registration or an applicable exemption.
